text:
Mavrik Bourque's first season in Nashville, after his trade from Dallas, still has no goal in it, 16 games in. Predlines put it plainly: "Predators are still waiting for Mavrik Bourque to break out." Friday in Vegas added a different headline, with Markerzone reporting that a Tomas Hertl hit on Bourque drew Ryan O'Reilly's wrath and that Player Safety may step in.

Our numbers read the drought as mostly bad luck. He has zero goals on 3.81 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and 31 shots, and his chance rate (0.88 expected goals per 60) is above last season's 0.82, when he scored 20 for the Stars. Goals tend to follow chances like that. The harder problem is the other end: Nashville's share of five-on-five expected goals is 8.6 points worse with him on the ice than without. His style is distinct, at least. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 19% of his setups coming from behind the net (8% for a typical forward) and 51% of his shots off the rush. He has four assists in his last ten games, eight of which Nashville won.
headline: Mavrik Bourque's goalless start, 16 games deep
